thread:
tess: Noticing p95 tail regressions for super-short streaming responses after the new short-kernel rollout. Host work looks to be the blocker now.
logan: saw same in dashboards. Can you post the quick flame snapshot?
tess: pasted: ```
flame: ingress_handler -> parse_stream -> ascii_quickcheck -> normalize_utf8_slow -> writev_flush_per_chunk -> grpc_write_small -> epoll_wait
hotspots: writev_flush_per_chunk (45%), normalize_utf8_slow (16%), grpc_write_small (14%)
```
devon: that writev_flush_per_chunk is killing us. Kernel improvements lowered GPU time so host syscall overhead is visible.
mira: two low-risk options: 1) re-introduce a host-side write aggregator (size/count/timeout knobs) to reduce syscalls; 2) add a fast-path for UTF-8 normalization so we avoid the full normalize for already-normalized inputs.
tess: microbench data: enabling aggregator (max_chunks=4, max_bytes=4096, timeout_ms=6) + utf8 fast-path drops p95 from 240ms -> 170ms for <=64-token streams. Syscalls per request down ~3.6x. Proxy CPU +5%.
logan: what's KV impact if we hold frames? Any chance of serializing more at kv-shard leaders?
devon: good call. If we delay flush and the request hits a KV miss, we could increase per-request kv serialization for multi-chunk flows. Baseline tests show typical 1-2 chunk requests unaffected, but heavy requests (10+ chunks) got ~5% higher kv latency in the first canary.
mira: propose default aggregator plus bypass rules: if chunk_count > 8 OR request.size > 80KB then flush immediately. Also for kv_miss paths use chunk_count > 5 threshold to bypass. Finally, add per-tenant opt-out flag for heavy streamers.
tess: added lightweight `is_nfc_fastcheck` heuristic that does a cheap scan for non-ascii combining marks; false-positive rate in bench <0.7%. Using that to skip normalize_utf8_slow.
logan: we need telemetry before wide rollout: histograms for `host.preproc.normalize_ms`, counters `host.streamer.writev_calls`, histo `host.streamer.agg_held_bytes`, and `host.streamer.agg_bypass_count` tagged by reason.
devon: added metrics to branch: ```
metrics.hist("host.preproc.normalize_ms", normalize_ms)
metrics.count("host.streamer.writev_calls", writev_calls)
metrics.histo("host.streamer.agg_held_bytes", agg_bytes)
metrics.tagged_count("host.streamer.agg_bypass_count", bypass_reason)
```
ops-bot: deploy streamer-miniagg-canary -> intake-4 (5%)
ops-bot: rollout started: 5% -> 100% in 12m if healthy
tess: initial 12m: canary p95 -19% vs baseline on short streams, writev_calls per-request -3.9x, normalize_ms median 0.09ms. One tenant with 25-chunk bursts saw kv latency +6%.
logan: tighten kv bypass for kv_miss to chunk_count > 4 just for canary hosts and add tenant opt-out.
devon: updated rule and rolled canary to 15%. Heavy-tenant metrics back to baseline; overall p95 still -16%.
mira: PR checklist: include microbench scripts, flame captures, default config flags `host.streamer.agg_bytes`, `host.streamer.agg_chunks`, `host.streamer.agg_timeout_ms`, `host.preproc.utf8_fastcheck=true`, `host.streamer.kv_bypass_chunk_threshold`, and per-tenant opt-out. Also add a short note in kernel-selection runbook: "validate host batching impact when short-seq kernels are used".
tess: scheduling 25m follow-up tomorrow 9:30am to finalize thresholds and prod rollout plan. labels: perf, host-parse, grpc, kvcache.
